title: Microsoft Edge: allow Microsoft 365 authentication pop-ups in work profiles
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly says no admin centre control or API is documented, although Microsoft documents Intune configuration and Graph setting updates. The policy paths, registry settings and default are supported, but the assurances about unchanged data access and storage are not.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not state how Edge determines the complete set of Microsoft first party sites for this exemption.
claims.quote: Searched: M365AuthPopupsInWorkEnabled first party sites data storage authentication popups; M365AuthPopupsInWorkEnabled Microsoft first party services full list sites criteria. Read policy, Intune What's new and Edge release notes; they give examples, not matching criteria or an exhaustive list.

claims.claim: No new data is read.
claims.quote: Searched: M365AuthPopupsInWorkEnabled data read stored privacy first party services list. Opened the policy and Intune What's new; they describe pop-up permission and sign-in, not whether additional data is read.
claims.fix: Remove 'No new data is read or stored.' Neither cited source establishes that assurance.

claims.claim: No new data is stored.
claims.quote: Searched: M365AuthPopupsInWorkEnabled data read stored privacy first party services list. Opened the policy and Intune What's new; neither states that this change stores no new data.
claims.fix: Remove 'No new data is read or stored.' Neither cited source establishes that assurance.

claims.claim: The policy does not change what Microsoft 365 sites can reach.
claims.quote: Searched: M365AuthPopupsInWorkEnabled data read stored privacy first party services list. Read the policy and Intune What's new; they establish the pop-up exemption, but do not state an unchanged data-access boundary.
claims.fix: Remove '; it does not change what the Microsoft 365 sites can reach'. Keep the supported statement that the policy changes whether Edge lets a pop-up window open.

claims.claim: The supplied sources describe a sign-in pop-up policy, not an agent or automated action.
claims.quote: Searched: M365AuthPopupsInWorkEnabled agent automated action roles prerequisites. Read the complete policy and roadmap description; neither describes an agent or an autonomous action.

claims.claim: The policy page names no administrator role or separate prerequisite.
claims.quote: Searched: M365AuthPopupsInWorkEnabled agent automated action roles prerequisites. Read the complete policy page: it gives supported browser versions and policy settings, but no administrator role or separate prerequisites section.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no admin centre switch for this pop-up policy.
claims.quote:
To see and configure these settings in Intune, create a Windows settings catalog profile
Microsoft Edge > Identity and sign-in > Allow M365 authentication popups in work profiles
claims.fix: Remove the sentence 'Microsoft Learn documents no admin centre switch or API for this policy at the time of writing (November 2026); the registry value and the macOS preference key are the documented automation surfaces.' Microsoft documents this setting in the Intune Windows settings catalog; the sentence is also ambiguous about which pop-up policy it means.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API for this pop-up policy.
claims.fix: Remove the same 'no admin centre switch or API' sentence. Microsoft documents Graph updates of Intune configuration settings, and its Intune documentation includes M365AuthPopupsInWorkEnabled in that settings catalog. Do not infer that no API exists from the policy reference listing registry and macOS settings.

claims.claim: A deployed policy applies its configured settings.
claims.quote:
If you enable this policy or don't configure it, Microsoft 365 authentication pop-ups are allowed in work profiles.
If you disable this policy, Microsoft 365 authentication pop-ups follow the default settings like other pop-ups.

claims.claim: An impact rating of medium fits the stated change to default browser behaviour.
claims.quote:
impact: "medium"
impact: Medium. Behaviour changes by default for people signed in to Edge with a work account
claims.fix: Set impact to 'high' and change the rationale's opening 'Medium.' to 'High.' The schema defines high impact as 'most users, or a change to default behaviour'; the stated rationale explicitly describes the latter.
